title: Taxonomy Field: Categories and Tags on Your Content

chapters.title: Taxonomy Field: Categories and Tags
chapters.subtitle: Attach the terms of a taxonomy to a content type

steps.text: A taxonomy holds the terms you sort content with. A Taxonomy Field attaches them to a content type, so editors can pick them. In this video, you add Category and Tags fields to Blog Post, use both, and see the terms on the site.

A taxonomy is a managed vocabulary, and this site has two, Categories and Tags. It is made of terms, and terms can sit inside other terms. A Taxonomy Field lets a content type use a taxonomy: you attach the field to the type.

Editors pick terms while they edit an item, and the field offers two editors. The Standard editor shows every term as a checkbox or a radio button. The Tags editor is a box where you type to search, and can create tags as you go.

Each field uses one taxonomy, and its settings define the rules for the selection: Required, Unique and Leaves only. The display mode, Standard or Tags, decides how the chosen terms appear on the page. Let's build one field of each kind on Blog Post.

chapters.title: Add a Category field
chapters.subtitle: The Standard editor, one term per post

steps.text: Content types are under Design, Content Definition, Content Types. Let's edit Blog Post, which has two fields here, a Subtitle and a Banner Image.
Add Field opens a form. The Display Name is what editors see, so let's type Category. The Technical Name fills in from it.
Field Type lists the kinds of field. Let's choose Taxonomy Field, and then Save & Configure, which saves the field and opens its settings.
Taxonomy is where the field draws its terms from, and Categories is the one to select. The Hint is a line of help that editors see with the field, so let's write one.
Required makes a selection mandatory, and it stays off here. Unique allows one term only, and Leaves only restricts the choice to terms with no children below them. Let's turn on both.
Below are two questions: What type of editor should be used? What type of display mode should be used? Both stay on Standard, and Save stores the settings.
Back on Blog Post, Category is listed as a Taxonomy Field, below the Subtitle and the Banner Image.

chapters.title: Add a Tags field
chapters.subtitle: The Tags editor and the Tags display mode

steps.text: Back on Blog Post, the Tags field starts the same way: Add Field, the Display Name Tags, the field type Taxonomy Field, and Save & Configure.

This time the Taxonomy is Tags, and Required, Unique and Leaves only stay off, so a post can have any number of tags. Placeholder replaces the text Type to search in the Tags editor, and the Standard editor ignores it. Let's leave it empty.
Next, let's set the editor question to Tags. One more setting appears, called Open, which lets editors create tags while they type.
The hint of Open notes that a tag created this way has only its display text. Let's leave Open on.
Let's also set the display mode question to Tags, so the page displays the field as tags. Save stores the settings.
Tags is listed with two badges, one for its display mode and one for its editor, both reading Tags. Category has none, because it uses the Standard ones.

chapters.title: Choose terms while editing
chapters.subtitle: Pick a category, pick and create tags

steps.text: This list of posts comes from the Blog menu. Edit opens the post A Night Train Across the Alps, and its Category and Tags fields are further down the page.
Category shows its Hint, then the terms of the Categories taxonomy as radio buttons, because Unique is on. Trains is indented under Travel.
Travel is disabled, because Leaves only restricts the choice to terms with no children. Let's select Trains.
Tags is a box with the placeholder Type to search. Let's type the first letters of Exploration, and select it from the list.
To create a tag, type a name that is not in the list. Let's type Night Train, and the box offers Press enter to create a tag.
Pressing Enter adds Night Train to the Tags taxonomy right away, and selects it. Only users with the Manage taxonomies permission can create tags this way.
Publish saves the post with its category and its two tags.

chapters.title: See the terms on the site
chapters.subtitle: The category and the tags as badges

steps.text: Back in the Blog list, View opens the post on the site.
Below the text, the category shows as a badge, and each tag as a badge of its own. The field stores the choice, and the theme's templates decide how it looks.
A Taxonomy Field attaches the terms of one taxonomy to a content type: the Standard editor shows every term, and the Tags editor lets you search for tags and create them. Thanks for watching.
